summary: Inventory all SolidStats skills, repo skill-state, and the estesis reference family; classify every section by stack-specificity

skillReports.name: solidstats-process-project-standards
skillReports.scope_claim: Every SolidStats repository (server-2, replays-fetcher, replay-parser-2, web, infrastructure) and every session. Defines "how work happens across the platform, not how any single stack is written."

sections.title: GSD Workflow Obligations
sections.gist: Mandates checking .planning/ docs before implementing, keeping them current, and using skills-first approach. The .planning/ layout and GSD workflow are SolidStats-specific conventions.

sections.title: Session Hygiene
sections.gist: End-of-session git commit discipline: commit all intended work, never fake a clean state by discarding incomplete work.

sections.title: Conventional Commits + Destructive Op Safety
sections.gist: Conventional Commits format with SolidStats-specific scope examples (phase numbers like 17-03). Git safety rules (no --no-verify, no amend-after-hook-failure) are universal doctrine but co-located here.

sections.title: Cross-App Boundary Map
sections.gist: Per-repo ownership table for all five SolidStats repos: what each owns and must not cross. Entirely SolidStats-specific topology.

sections.title: Cross-App Compatibility Protocol
sections.gist: Risk-based checklist of cross-repo contract surfaces (API shape, DB schema, RabbitMQ message, S3 key layout, parser contract, auth shape, moderation workflow) that require verification before implementation.

sections.title: Security Minimums
sections.gist: No secrets in logs/commits, no hardcoded env values, env-var validation at startup (envalid for Node, config struct for Rust), pre-commit .env/.gitignore check. Mostly universal doctrine with repo-specific tool names.

sections.title: Risk Management Protocol
sections.gist: Procedure for risky requests: explain, propose safer alternatives, require explicit confirmation. References §D/§E boundaries and .planning/PROJECT.md — making it SolidStats-specific despite a universal underlying principle.

sections.title: Documentation Language
sections.gist: English for code/comments/planning docs; Russian for GSD session replies; bilingual EN+RU mandatory for skill trigger phrases. Specific to this team's bilingual RU/EN context.

sections.title: MCP Usage Guidelines
sections.gist: Context7 as primary library docs MCP with a per-repo library lookup table (Fastify/TypeBox/Kysely for server-2, tokio/lapin for replay-parser-2, TanStack/ark-ui for web, etc.). ToolSearch deferred-load pattern for Claude Code + subagent contexts.

sections.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Shape + Concurrency
sections.gist: Single cd.yml per repo, verify→image job topology, concurrency block with cancel-in-progress. The exact structure is standard CI doctrine but the specific job names and conditions are SolidStats conventions.

sections.title: Verify Job — TypeScript repos
sections.gist: pnpm 11 + Node 25, frozen lockfile, Docker Compose services (PG 17, RabbitMQ 4, MinIO), prettier+eslint+tsc+test+integration+coverage (V8, 100% gates). Applies to server-2 and replays-fetcher.

sections.title: Verify Job — Rust repo
sections.gist: Rust 1.95.0, dtolnay/rust-toolchain, Swatinem/rust-cache, fmt+clippy -D warnings+test. Applies to replay-parser-2 only.

sections.title: Docker Image Build + GHCR Push
sections.gist: docker/metadata-action with sha+branch tags, push to ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}, runs only on non-PR pushes after verify passes.

sections.title: Dockerfile Conventions (TS + Rust)
sections.gist: Multi-stage builds: Node 25 Alpine for TS services, rust:1.95.0-bookworm builder + debian:bookworm-slim runtime for Rust. Non-root UID 65532:65532, pnpm frozen install, explicit EXPOSE.

sections.where: references/ci-cd-pattern.md — Local services via Docker Compose
sections.title: Docker Compose Test Services
sections.gist: Standard service layout: postgres:17-alpine, rabbitmq:4-management-alpine, minio/minio with host-port offset convention (e.g. 15432 instead of 5432).

sections.title: Infrastructure Repo CI/CD (validate + SSH deploy)
sections.gist: Separate validate+deploy topology for the infrastructure repo: Python manifest validation, SSH-based kubectl apply, GitHub environment protection for staging, SHA pinning enforcement via validate-staging.py.

skillReports.naming_fit: Name parses cleanly as solidstats-process-<target>-<purpose>: 'process' signals workflow/process rules, 'project' signals cross-repo/platform scope, 'standards' signals the normative baseline. No semantic mismatch — the skill genuinely covers platform-wide process rather than any single stack.
overlaps_suspected: solidstats-process-ts-standards — both cover TypeScript-repo CI tooling (pnpm, Node version, test commands); the verify-job TS section in ci-cd-pattern.md partially duplicates what solidstats-process-ts-standards likely mandates for the pnpm/test pipeline

Any future solidstats-stack-rust-* skill — the Rust verify job and Dockerfile conventions in ci-cd-pattern.md (cargo fmt/clippy flags, Rust version, debian-slim base) belong to the Rust stack layer, not the cross-project process layer

solidstats-process-backend-standards (WIP) — §F security minimums (env-var validation, no-secrets-in-logs) are exactly the kind of rules a backend-standards skill would repeat; risk of duplication if that skill also restates startup-fail-fast and envalid/config-struct patterns
skillReports.notes:
1. §C mixes two distinct concerns: the Conventional Commits format (repo-specific due to scope examples like '17-03') and git safety rules (no --no-verify, no amend-after-hook-failure) that are universal doctrine and arguably belong in a universal-doctrine layer or even in the global CLAUDE.md. The git safety rules duplicate what the Claude Code harness instructions already say.

2. §I (MCP Usage) is the most load-bearing section for day-to-day agent behavior, but it is also the most likely to drift — the per-repo library table (specific versions, specific packages) is maintenance-heavy and lives in a 'process' skill rather than in per-stack skills where library lists are more naturally maintained.

3. references/ci-cd-pattern.md conflates four distinct stack concerns into one file: TS CI, Rust CI, shared Docker/GHCR push pattern, and infrastructure SSH-deploy pattern. A taxonomy redesign should split this into stack-specific references owned by each stack skill, keeping only the shared job topology (concurrency block, verify→image gate) in this process skill.

4. §D (Cross-App Boundary Map) is the single highest-value section — it is genuinely cross-cutting and belongs here. It would be a mistake to move it to any per-stack skill.

5. §G references §D and .planning/PROJECT.md, creating an implicit hard-require on §D and on the GSD planning-doc convention — but no formal hard_requires are declared, which is fine since both are in this same skill.

6. The skill declares 'over-triggering is acceptable' in its description, which is appropriate given it's the universal baseline, but this means it will be loaded on every SolidStats task — the weight of §I (MCP) and ci-cd-pattern.md adds significant token cost per invocation. Splitting the CI/CD reference into per-stack skills would reduce this cost without losing coverage.

skillReports.name: solidstats-process-ts-standards
skillReports.scope_claim: Baseline TypeScript / Node.js standards shared by every SolidStats TypeScript project (server-2, replays-fetcher, web). Explicitly excludes replay-parser-2 (Rust).

sections.title: tsconfig Strictness Baseline
sections.gist: Mandatory tsconfig flags (strict + 10 additional checks) and module/target settings applied identically to all three SolidStats TS repos. Includes Node vs. web frontend target split as inline comments.

sections.title: TypeScript Code Style
sections.gist: type over interface, no any, no non-null assertions, no unexplained as casts, import type, import ordering, and Record<Enum,…> pattern for exhaustive lookup tables — all enforced by ESLint and code review.

sections.title: ESLint Baseline — Node Repos (server-2, replays-fetcher)
sections.gist: ESLint 10 flat config with typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked, unicorn, and import-x for Node repos only; web frontend uses Oxlint via Vite+ instead. Includes specific rule set and rationale.

sections.title: Runtime & Toolchain
sections.gist: Node.js 25, pnpm 11, ESM with NodeNext resolution, tsx for dev execution, Prettier 3.x with default config — pinned to specific versions used across all three SolidStats TS repos.

sections.title: Test Toolchain & Coverage Gates
sections.gist: Vitest 4 + @vitest/coverage-v8, 100% coverage thresholds on all metrics (non-advisory), unit/integration test file naming conventions, Testcontainers for real deps, and required npm script names.

skillReports.naming_fit: Name parses as solidstats-process-ts-standards. The 'process' segment is unexpected — the skill is a standards/conventions reference, not a workflow process (no steps, gates, or decision flows). The peer skills use 'backend-ts-conventions' and 'frontend-react-conventions' naming; 'process' here appears to be a namespace used for cross-cutting standards docs rather than a framework-specific conventions skill. Mild semantic mismatch: 'process' implies a procedural guide but the content is purely declarative standards.
overlaps_suspected: solidstats-backend-ts-conventions: §B (TypeScript code style) and §C (ESLint baseline) were explicitly extracted from that skill per CHANGELOG — risk of drift if either skill is updated independently.
solidstats-frontend-react-conventions: §8 per CHANGELOG was the other extraction source — same drift risk for tsconfig and test toolchain sections.
solidstats-process-project-standards: likely overlaps on Node version, pnpm version, and Prettier — project-level toolchain pins are natural territory for a project-standards skill.
skillReports.notes:
1. §C explicitly splits Node repos from the web frontend mid-section ('web uses Oxlint via Vite+ instead'), making the section boundary misleading — the section title says 'ESLint Baseline' but it silently defers web linting to a different tool. This split belongs in a classification note or a separate §C-web section.

2. §D mixes two distinct concerns: runtime pins (Node 25, pnpm 11, ESM) which are repo-specific SolidStats decisions, and formatting (Prettier 3.x defaults) which is closer to universal-doctrine. Splitting these would sharpen taxonomy.

3. §E's Testcontainers bullet ('Never mock the database or queue at the contract boundary') is substantive integration-test doctrine that could be universal-doctrine; it's currently buried in what reads as a toolchain section.

4. The skill claims to be hard-required by solidstats-backend-ts-conventions and solidstats-frontend-react-conventions, but it declares no hard_requires itself, which is consistent and correct.

5. The 100% coverage gate is stated as 'enforced, not advisory' but the carve-out logic ('what is legitimately excluded is defined by per-stack skills') means the gate is only enforced in combination with those skills — the standalone skill gives an incomplete picture.

6. The tsconfig block in §A embeds both Node and web frontend target variants as inline comments inside the same snippet, which creates ambiguity when reading for a single repo. A taxonomy redesign should split tsconfig content by stack layer.

skillReports.name: solidstats-process-review-standards
skillReports.scope_claim: Shared review foundation for every SolidStats code-review skill — backend, parser, and frontend alike (server-2, replays-fetcher, replay-parser-2, web). Not a standalone reviewer; consumed by solidstats-backend-ts-code-review, solidstats-parser-rust-code-review, solidstats-frontend-react-code-review.

sections.title: Review philosophy
sections.gist: Seven cross-cutting principles: directness, signal over volume, evidence before opinion, pedantry discipline, risk-first ordering, code-not-author framing, and read-only default. Nothing is stack- or language-specific.

sections.title: Establishing scope
sections.gist: Defines how to resolve what is in scope (named base > staged > branch diff), the read-full-file rule, the constraint that numbered findings must point at changed/relied-on lines, and the out-of-scope pre-existing note pattern. The git commands given are universal; the TS sample paths are illustrative only.

sections.title: Severity buckets
sections.gist: Defines the single-axis severity scale (🔴 Blocker / 🟠 High / 🟡 Medium / 🔵 Low), verdict mapping per bucket, calibration rules, and translation from older word/label scales. Fully stack-agnostic.

sections.title: Output format
sections.gist: Mandates English-only report language (explicit divergence from the estesis standard which uses Russian) and the exact markdown report template with continuous numbering, topic tags, optional convention references, and section presence rules. The English mandate is a SolidStats-family-specific policy, not a universal doctrine.

sections.title: Verdict rules
sections.gist: Mechanical derivation of APPROVE / REQUEST CHANGES / BLOCK from the highest-severity finding, including the hard-gate BLOCK override. Fully stack-agnostic.

sections.title: Test files
sections.gist: Rules for severity of test-quality findings: never standalone BLOCK, poor quality is at most REQUEST CHANGES, test that masks a real bug is 🔴, missing tests for branching logic are 🟡. No stack dependency.

sections.title: Noise filter — what NOT to report
sections.gist: Seven categories of non-findings to suppress: subjective naming, code matching repo conventions, speculative security, ungrounded performance, missing tests for untouched code, auto-formatter output, linter echo. Fully stack-agnostic.

sections.title: If asked to fix
sections.gist: Read-only default with four constraints when fixing is explicitly requested: smallest change, follow project conventions, one fix per finding, re-run gates. Stack-agnostic.

skillReports.naming_fit: Name parses cleanly as solidstats-process-review-standards: solidstats = family scope, process = meta/cross-cutting layer (not tied to one stack), review-standards = purpose. Accurate — the skill is a process foundation, not a stack convention file.
overlaps_suspected: estesis-process-review-standards: CHANGELOG confirms this skill was directly adapted from estesis-process-review-standards with minimal changes (severity buckets, output format, verdict rules, scope discipline, test-file rule, noise filter all copied verbatim). The two skills share essentially the same body; the only material divergence is the English-vs-Russian report language mandate. If a universal review-foundation skill ever existed, both would become thin wrappers over it.
skillReports.notes:
1. The skill is almost entirely universal doctrine, yet it lives in the solidstats family namespace. Sections A, B, C, E, F, G, H are all stack-agnostic and could be promoted to a cross-family universal skill. Only the English-language mandate in §D is SolidStats-specific (estesis uses Russian). The output format template itself (markdown shape, numbering, topic tags) is also universal-doctrine except for that one language rule.

2. CHANGELOG explicitly states it was adapted from estesis-process-review-standards with near-verbatim copy. This is the strongest signal for a taxonomy redesign: a single universal-process-review-standards skill with a language/locale knob, and thin family wrappers (solidstats, estesis) that override only the language setting and name the concrete reviewer skills.

3. No references/, workflows/, or templates/ subdirectories exist — the skill is entirely self-contained in SKILL.md.

4. The skill correctly sets hard_requires = [] (it is itself the base layer; the reviewers require it, not the other way around).

5. §D's output format template uses `.ts` sample file paths (a minor TS lean in an otherwise universal template) and mentions Clippy as a convention-reference example — the only Rust-specific token, added during the estesis→solidstats adaptation. These are illustrative and do not make the section stack-specific.

6. The description explicitly states this skill should NOT be triggered for an actual review, only for meta questions about the standard. This is load-bearing for triggering hygiene — the child reviewer skills must hard-require it without triggering it as a standalone reviewer.

skillReports.name: solidstats-process-testing-standards
skillReports.scope_claim: Shared testing foundation for every SolidStats stack — backend (TS/Fastify), parser (Rust), and frontend (React/TanStack) alike. Owns the stack-agnostic testing philosophy. Per-stack skills hard-require this skill and read it first.

sections.title: The RITE standard
sections.gist: Defines the RITE (Readable, Isolated, Thorough, Explicit) quality bar for any test. Stack-agnostic — applies equally to TS, Rust, and any other stack.

sections.title: Unit vs integration boundary
sections.gist: Draws the unit/integration line on behavioral scope, not call count; mandates real ephemeral dependencies (testcontainers / Docker Compose) over mocks at contract boundaries (DB, queue, S3, HTTP). Language-agnostic principle, though concrete harness names are delegated to per-stack skills.

sections.title: AAA (Arrange / Act / Assert)
sections.gist: Mandates Arrange/Act/Assert structure in every test and the DRY rule for Arrange/Assert shared values. No language or runner assumptions.

sections.title: Naming
sections.gist: Test names must describe behavior and expected result; provides formula templates. Casing guidance is tied to natural-language sentence start, not any language convention.

sections.title: Determinism and flakiness
sections.gist: Defines determinism, enumerates common flakiness causes (timers, shared state, locale leakage, unseeded randomness), and bans reruns as a fix. Fully stack-agnostic.

sections.title: Test doubles
sections.gist: Establishes the classic Dummy/Stub/Fake/Spy/Mock vocabulary, guidance on when to use each, and the over-mocking anti-pattern. No runner- or language-specific APIs mentioned.

sections.title: Oracle strength and assertions
sections.gist: Defines a strong oracle and bans trivial assertions, snapshot noise for unstable output, and assertions that mirror implementation steps.

sections.title: Coverage and mutation mindset
sections.gist: Directs maximizing coverage with justified exceptions; distinguishes structural coverage (floor) from mutation testing (oracle quality); explicitly delegates numeric thresholds and tooling to per-stack skills.

sections.title: Scope and realism
sections.gist: Requires testing through public API surface only; forbids exports added solely for tests; treats inability to reach behavior through the public API as an architecture signal.

sections.title: TDD (Red-Green-Refactor)
sections.gist: Recommends TDD as default workflow (Red-Green-Refactor cycle), explicitly not a merge gate. Stack-agnostic discipline.

sections.title: What the per-stack skills own
sections.gist: Delegation map: runner & invocation, file placement, language idioms, integration harness, coverage tool + threshold, and specialized testing (fuzz) are all owned by per-stack skills. This section is itself stack-agnostic governance.

sections.title: Review checklist
sections.gist: Eight-point checklist for writing/reviewing tests; references §B for integration boundary rule. Fully language-independent.

skillReports.naming_fit: Name parses as solidstats-process-{testing-standards}. The 'process' segment is slightly odd — the skill is closer to universal doctrine than a workflow process — but it mirrors the sibling naming convention (solidstats-process-project-standards, solidstats-process-ts-standards). No semantic mismatch; the name accurately signals it is a standards/doctrine document rather than an action-oriented workflow skill.
overlaps_suspected: solidstats-process-ts-standards — may contain TS-specific test style rules (e.g. Vitest idioms, file co-location) that duplicate or conflict with what §K delegates to the per-stack test skills; exact overlap cannot be confirmed without reading that skill

estesis-frontend-react-unit-tests (mentioned in CHANGELOG as the origin of RITE/AAA/naming/determinism/doubles/oracle/coverage/TDD content) — if that skill still exists and is loaded, doctrine sections A-J are duplicated there
skillReports.notes:
1. Every section is genuinely universal-doctrine — there is not a single ts-shared, stack-specific, or repo-specific rule in the file. The skill correctly defers all concrete tooling (runner, file layout, threshold numbers, fuzz harness) to per-stack skills via §K.

2. The skill self-describes as 'not a standalone test-writer' and lists meta-only triggers, which is correct — but this means it will never be triggered directly by a developer writing tests. Its only activation path is being hard-required by the per-stack test skills. The description should confirm those per-stack skill names once they are created (solidstats-backend-ts-tests, solidstats-parser-rust-tests, solidstats-frontend-react-tests are named but may not exist yet).

Section B mentions testcontainers and Docker Compose test services as the preferred integration harness — these are implementation examples that technically belong to per-stack skills, but their appearance here is acceptable as illustrative examples supporting the doctrine rather than prescriptive tooling rules.

skillReports.name: solidstats-process-backend-standards
skillReports.scope_claim: Shared service-side standards for every SolidStats TypeScript service — server-2 (Fastify HTTP backend) and replays-fetcher (ingest CLI). Owns stack-neutral rules both inherit: naming and factory contracts, typed error system (base), enums/constants, config & validated-input discipline, external adapters, async safety, process lifecycle, LSP, SOLID/DRY thresholds, utility libraries, observability (§Z), log diagnosability (§AA), and resource lifecycle (§AB). Explicitly does NOT cover web (React/TanStack) or replay-parser-2 (Rust).

sections.title: Naming
sections.gist: File kebab-case with role suffix, PascalCase contracts, factory function pattern (create…), camelCase variables, UPPER_SNAKE for constants, no I-prefix on interfaces, domain identifier conventions (steamId64, entityId).

sections.title: Typed error system (base)
sections.gist: Mandatory abstract AppError base class with code/message/details/cause fields; errors defined per module in <feature>.errors.ts; domain vs ExternalServiceError taxonomy; transport mapping delegated to per-stack skills.

sections.title: Enums & constants
sections.gist: No TS enum; use as-const object + derived union type; compare against the const object, never raw magic strings; repeated literals live in a per-module const.

sections.title: Config & validated input discipline
sections.gist: Validate env/config once at boot and fail fast; no per-environment branching on NODE_ENV; no hardcoded secrets; schema-first types derived from runtime schema (TypeBox or Zod); all externally-sourced fields bounded.

sections.title: External adapters
sections.gist: Clients created once and injected; connection failure vs non-2xx upstream mapped to distinct error types; auth headers built by a helper; upstream status/body snippet logged on error; long-lived clients configured with timeouts and connection limits.

sections.title: Async safety
sections.gist: No blocking sync I/O on async paths; no N+1 per-item awaits inside loops; independent operations run concurrently; no floating promises; external I/O has a timeout and AbortSignal threading.

sections.title: Process lifecycle & construction
sections.gist: No module-level state with side effects (client/config/singleton at import time); composition in factory/composition root; graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT with forced-exit timeout.

sections.title: Contract compliance (LSP)
sections.gist: Factories implementing a contract must not defeat the type checker via as-cast or ts-expect-error; no widening return types or adding required params callers cannot supply; thrown errors must be a documented subset.

sections.title: SOLID thresholds
sections.gist: SRP: functions ≤~40 lines, factories ≤~5 non-structural deps; OCP: no if/else-if dispatch over 3+ branches — use a typed map instead.

sections.title: DRY — rule of three
sections.gist: Same logic (not merely similar shape) repeated 3+ times within a module must be extracted; similar-looking code across entities is acceptable.

sections.title: Utility & type libraries
sections.gist: Prescribes es-toolkit (runtime utilities), type-fest (type-level), day.js (dates), nanoid (non-DB IDs) over hand-rolled equivalents; source-of-truth types still derive from TypeBox/Zod schemas.

sections.title: §Z. Observability — log hygiene
sections.gist: Structured-only logging with correlation fields (replayId/jobId); log levels carry semantic meaning; state transitions must be logged; no PII/secrets/full rows in logs. Operational metrics surface (prom-client, /health vs run-summary) delegated to per-stack skills.

sections.title: §AA. Log diagnosability
sections.gist: Logs must allow post-hoc reconstruction of flow without a debugger: silent catch swallowing (🟠), traceback preservation, identifying context in errors (🟡), upstream failure detail (🟡), happy-path flow legibility (🔵). Defines boundary-logging contracts for each stack to avoid double-logging noise.

sections.title: §AB. Resource lifecycle — unbounded growth
sections.gist: Three-leg test: resource outlives request/run item + unbounded write path + no removal/cap. Covers in-memory accumulation (Map/Set/array on singletons), DB rows without retention/TTL, and files/objects never cleaned. Severity 🟠 default, 🔴 on hot path.

sections.title: Code-quality bugs
sections.gist: No silent catch, no identical branches, null checked before access, no console.* in prod, no TODO without tracker, error chaining preserved, no setTimeout-as-sleep, no any/as-dodge, exhaustive switch with never assertion.

sections.title: Comments & docs
sections.gist: English only; comments explain why not what; public contracts have doc comments; no commented-out code or narration comments.

sections.title: Imports & lint
sections.gist: ESLint all + typescript-eslint strict-type-checked + unicorn + import-x + Prettier; clean lint/typecheck required; index.ts exports only public contract; no wildcard imports of module internals; eslint-disable must carry justification comment.

skillReports.name: solidstats-backend-ts-conventions
skillReports.scope_claim: Primary subject: server-2 (Fastify 5, TypeBox, Kysely/pg, amqplib, S3, pino, prom-client, envalid). Shared baseline: replays-fetcher (commander CLI; Zod, no Fastify/amqplib). Fastify/TypeBox/HTTP sections tagged [HTTP] and do not bind the CLI. Does not cover replay-parser-2 (Rust) or web (React).

sections.title: 4-layer architecture and module layout
sections.gist: Defines controller→usecase→service→repository layering with downward-only dependencies, optional usecase layer, cross-module sharing only via exported service contracts, and the flat role-file module layout under src/modules/<feature>/. The layer pattern is TS/Node-idiomatic but not Fastify-specific — it could apply to replays-fetcher or another TS backend.

sections.title: Naming conventions: files, types, factories, identifiers
sections.gist: Prescribes kebab-case role-suffix filenames, PascalCase contracts with no I-prefix, camelCase functions, UPPER_SNAKE constants, factory-function pattern (createX returning typed type X), and SolidStats-specific identifiers (steamId64, replayId, jobId). The steamId64/replayId identifiers are repo-specific; the factory and naming rules are ts-shared in spirit but classified repo-specific because they are anchored to SolidStats domain identifiers.

sections.title: Fastify route/controller layer rules
sections.gist: Routes are Fastify plugins (FastifyPluginAsyncTypebox); every route requires TypeBox request + response schema; handler calls exactly one usecase/service; path comes from a RoutePath const; routes plugin carries prefix + OpenAPI tag. All rules are Fastify-specific and tagged [HTTP].

sections.title: Usecase layer: orchestration and transaction ownership
sections.gist: Usecases are justified only when orchestrating multiple services; they own the transaction boundary (db.transaction()); they depend on service contracts not concrete factories; no re-validation of service output; no no-op try/catch. The concept is framework-agnostic and applies equally to a CLI.

sections.title: Service layer rules
sections.gist: Services call repositories, return Value.Parse-validated domain data, raise only typed AppError subclasses, propagate tx handle to repositories. The TypeBox Value.Parse detail is server-2-specific; the Zod equivalent applies to replays-fetcher — the rule is effectively ts-shared.

sections.title: Repository layer rules
sections.gist: Repositories use Kysely query builder with no string-interpolated SQL; pagination via shared paginate helper; accept optional tx via tx ?? db pattern; return DB row types not domain schemas. Tied to Kysely/pg — replays-fetcher has no DB layer, so this is stack-specific to server-2.

sections.title: DI via Fastify plugins and app.decorate
sections.gist: Cross-cutting clients provided by src/infra/ fp-wrapped plugins with app.decorate; module layers wired in module plugins; no module-level singletons; long-lived shared clients created once in their plugin. Entirely Fastify-specific ([HTTP] scope).

sections.title: Typed error hierarchy (AppError + ExternalServiceError)
sections.gist: Abstract AppError with code/httpStatus/details/cause; per-module error files; one central setErrorHandler; consistent response envelope. The httpStatus + central Fastify handler wiring is stack-specific, but the AppError class design and error taxonomy apply to both TS repos — ts-shared is the better classification for the core hierarchy.

sections.title: TypeBox request/response schema discipline
sections.gist: Derive types via Static<typeof Schema>; bound every string/array/number on request bodies; additionalProperties:false; naming convention XBase/XFull/XCreate/XUpdate/XRow; response schema mandatory on every route. Tagged [HTTP]; replays-fetcher uses Zod — the principles carry over but the TypeBox API does not.

sections.title: Kysely database typing, migrations, transactions
sections.gist: Typed Database interface; consistent createdAt/updatedAt; migration discipline (up+down, backfill for NOT NULL, descriptive names, run via migrate.ts); explicit pg.Pool config; transaction boundary at usecase level. Entirely server-2/Kysely/pg stack — not applicable to replays-fetcher.

sections.title: Enum/const pattern: as const object + derived union
sections.gist: TypeScript has no StrEnum; use const object + derived union type; compare against const values not string literals; per-module RoutePath const. The pattern is a TS language idiom applicable to all SolidStats TS repos.

sections.title: Shared Pagination/Paged types and composable filter helpers
sections.gist: Shared Pagination type, paginate helper, Paged<T> result; composable $call(applyXFilter(f)) helpers; typed orderBy union. The $call Kysely-specific syntax and the shared helper tie this to server-2's Kysely stack.

sections.title: envalid-based config, no process.env scatter, no NODE_ENV branching
sections.gist: Validate env once at boot with envalid, expose via config decorator; no process.env reads scattered in code; no per-environment config objects; no hardcoded secrets. The envalid library and app.config decorator are server-2-specific details, but the principle (validate-once, no scatter, no secrets) is ts-shared.

sections.title: External HTTP adapter error taxonomy
sections.gist: Network failure → AppError (502); upstream non-2xx → ExternalServiceError; auth headers via helper not inline; log status + body snippet before raising. The taxonomy distinction is a design principle applicable to any TS backend calling external APIs.

sections.title: Event-loop safety: no blocking I/O, no N+1, no floating promises, timeouts/AbortSignal
sections.gist: No sync fs/hashing on async paths; no per-item await in loops (batch queries instead); concurrent ops via Promise.all; no floating promises (ESLint enforced); external I/O has timeout + AbortSignal. These are universal Node.js async rules, ts-shared at minimum.

sections.title: IDOR ownership check, mass assignment prevention
sections.gist: Every entity-id endpoint needs a visible ownership/role check; XCreate/XUpdate schemas must not accept server-assigned fields (steamId64, role, isAdmin, status). The IDOR and mass-assignment patterns are universal web API security principles but manifested in SolidStats domain terms (steamId64, isAdmin).

sections.title: HTTP hardening: rate-limit, helmet/CORS, bodyLimit, graceful shutdown, auth/session/CSRF
sections.gist: Fastify-specific plugins: @fastify/rate-limit, @fastify/helmet, @fastify/cors allow-list, bodyLimit; SIGTERM/SIGINT + app.close(); @fastify/under-pressure; Steam OAuth state/CSRF; HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite cookies. Entirely Fastify [HTTP] stack and server-2 domain (Steam OAuth, bounty/moderation routes).

sections.title: amqplib queue consumer discipline: manual ack, prefetch/QoS, DLQ, idempotency
sections.gist: Manual ack (no auto-ack), prefetch/QoS cap, dead-letter + delivery-count cap, idempotent writes for bounty/moderation mutations. Tied to server-2's amqplib/RabbitMQ parse_jobs queue — repo-specific.

sections.title: Factory/contract compliance: no as-cast widening, no surprise error types
sections.gist: Factory implementations must honor their contract type exactly; no as-cast to force satisfaction; no widening return types; thrown errors are a documented subset. A consequence of the factory-based contract pattern — ts-shared.

sections.title: SRP (40-line / 5-dep limits) and OCP (typed map over if/else chains)
sections.gist: Functions ≤40 lines; factories ≤5 non-structural deps; if/else chains >3 branches on a union replaced with typed Record map. These thresholds are SolidStats conventions but the principle is stack-agnostic — classified ts-shared.

sections.title: Extract duplicated logic only at 3+ occurrences
sections.gist: Extract the same logic (not similar shape) when repeated 3+ times within a module; similar-looking code across different entities is acceptable. This is a universal software principle.

sections.title: Prefer es-toolkit, type-fest, day.js, nanoid over hand-rolled helpers
sections.gist: Use es-toolkit for runtime collection/function utilities, type-fest for type derivation, day.js for date handling (UTC at boundary), nanoid for application-level ids. Tied to the SolidStats TS repos' approved dependency set — ts-shared across server-2 and replays-fetcher.

sections.title: Request schema bounds (maxLength/maxItems/min/max) and no business rules in schemas
sections.gist: Unbounded strings/arrays on request bodies are DoS vectors; business rules belong in the service as typed errors, not schema keywords. The principle is universal; the TypeBox specifics are stack-specific, but the equivalent applies to Zod in replays-fetcher — ts-shared overall.

sections.title: Structured pino logging hygiene: levels, state transitions, no PII/secrets, metrics
sections.gist: Structured logging via pino (log.info({ replayId, jobId }, 'msg')); log level semantics; state transitions logged; no PII/full-row logs; prom-client metrics for queue depth/job results/health endpoint. Pino and prom-client are server-2's specific tooling; the principle of structured logging is ts-shared but the implementation detail (pino, prom-client, /health) is stack-specific.

sections.title: Diagnosable logs: no silent catch, traceback preserved, identifying context in errors, upstream failure logging
sections.gist: Silent catch (no log + no rethrow) is 🟠; log error object not just message; errors carry identifying context (id, steamId64); upstream failures log status+body snippet. The guardrails reference Fastify's req.log and setErrorHandler boundary as already-covered, but the core rules are framework-agnostic operational hygiene.

sections.title: Detecting in-memory, DB row, and disk resource leaks
sections.gist: Three-leg finding criteria: resource outlives request + unbounded write path + no removal/cap. Covers module-level Map/Set growth, DB rows without retention/TTL, temp files without cleanup. Stack-agnostic reasoning applicable to any long-lived process.

sections.title: Code-quality micro-rules: empty catch, null checks, no console.*, error chaining, no any/as
sections.gist: No empty catch; null checked before access; no console.* in production; preserve error cause chain; no any/no as; exhaustive switch with never assertion. These are TypeScript-specific idioms applicable across all TS repos.

sections.title: Comment discipline: English only, why not what, doc public contracts, no commented-out code
sections.gist: Comments explain why; public contract types carry a short doc comment; no commented-out code or narration comments. Universal clean-code doctrine.

sections.title: ESLint/Prettier/tsc toolchain gate and import discipline
sections.gist: ESLint all + typescript-eslint strict-type-checked + unicorn + import-x + Prettier; tsc --noEmit required clean; index.ts re-exports only public contract; no wildcard imports; eslint-disable needs justification comment. Specific to the SolidStats TS toolchain setup — ts-shared.

sections.gist: Byte-identical artifact output required on every run/machine: BTreeMap/sorted Vec only, no SystemTime/rand/env in derived data, float epsilon, serde_json float_roundtrip for parse-side canonicalization, overflow-checks=true in release, RFC 8785 JCS note for hashing, total stable sort key.

sections.gist: thiserror everywhere (no anyhow), one typed error enum per crate/module, propagate with ?, C-GOOD-ERR bounds (Error + Send + Sync + 'static, lowercase Display), #[from]/#[source] for cause chains.

Covers cargo test runner, manifest-driven golden/parity harness, determinism tests, proptest, insta snapshots, cargo-fuzz, and coverage gate.

sections.title: Runner & layout
sections.gist: Uses cargo test / cargo nextest, co-located #[cfg(test)] mod tests for units, integration tests in crates/<crate>/tests/, and the golden/parity harness in crates/parser-core/tests/. Tests return Result and use ? over unwrap; assert error variants with matches!.

sections.title: Determinism test (first-class)
sections.gist: The deterministic_output test asserts byte-identical artifact output across runs and threads, guarding the determinism convention (§C of solidstats-parser-rust-conventions). Every new derived field must be added to it.

sections.title: Golden / parity harness
sections.gist: Manifest-driven harness at crates/parser-core/tests/ maps fixtures to requirement/decision IDs and expected status/features. Every new parsing behavior or decision gets a fixture and manifest entry; schema_drift_status and fault_injection_regressions are always kept green.

sections.title: Property testing with proptest
sections.gist: Mandates proptest for roundtrip (parse(serialize(a))==a), invariants (determinism, ordering stability, status monotonicity), and the 'malformed input never panics' property. Requires committing proptest-regressions/ to source control. Model-based proptest for worker orchestration is a medium-priority recommendation.

sections.title: Snapshot testing with insta
sections.gist: Uses insta (assert_json_snapshot!) on representative fixtures with minimal redactions. Enforces CI=true auto-fail on drift and --unreferenced=auto; local workflow is cargo insta review.

sections.title: Fuzzing with cargo-fuzz
sections.gist: Requires two fuzz targets: raw &[u8] decode and structure-aware via #[derive(Arbitrary)] on the IR. Seed corpus committed from golden fixtures, minimized with cargo fuzz cmin; CI smoke run with -max_total_time=300 (libFuzzer flag, must follow --); cargo fuzz coverage to close the loop.

sections.title: Contract tests
sections.gist: parser-contract types validated against the published JSON Schema via the jsonschema crate; schema drift is a CI failure. A C-DEBUG-NONEMPTY test asserts every public contract type's Debug output is non-empty.

sections.title: Coverage gate
sections.gist: cargo-llvm-cov through parser-quality + scripts/coverage-gate.sh; aims toward 100% reachable in parser-core. Coverage is treated as a floor, not proof — paired with property and fuzz layers.

skillReports.naming_fit: solidstats-parser-rust-tests parses cleanly as solidstats (family) - parser (scope: replay-parser-2) - rust (stack) - tests (purpose). No semantic mismatch; the name precisely matches the content.
overlaps_suspected: solidstats-process-testing-standards: owns testing philosophy (RITE, AAA, unit-vs-integration boundary, determinism doctrine, doubles, oracle strength, coverage mindset, TDD) — this skill explicitly delegates to it; the boundary is clear but a reviewer must read both to get the full picture

solidstats-parser-rust-conventions §C (determinism) and §F (totality) and §G (contract) — those sections define the invariants that the tests here verify; the conceptual rules live there, the test enforcement lives here; split is intentional but cross-referencing is required
skillReports.notes:
1. Only two files exist (SKILL.md + CHANGELOG.md) — no references/, workflows/, or templates/ subdirectories. The skill is self-contained and fairly thin by design (it explicitly delegates philosophy to solidstats-process-testing-standards and conventions to solidstats-parser-rust-conventions).

2. The 'malformed input never panics' property test rule (proptest section) is arguably universal-doctrine for any parser handling untrusted input, not Rust-specific. It's classified stack-specific here only because it's expressed as a proptest pattern and tied to Rust's Result/panic model.

3. The two-fuzz-target strategy (raw bytes + structure-aware via Arbitrary) is a strong, well-motivated pattern that could be extracted into a generic 'parser fuzzing doctrine' if a second Rust parser ever joins the family.

4. The CHANGELOG references .planning/RESEARCH-parser-cluster.md and .planning/SKILLS-ANALYSIS.md as upstream rationale sources — those files are not in this skill directory and would need to be found in the broader repo if audit depth requires it.

5. The coverage-gate section references an external 'coverage-analysis' skill and the cargo-fuzz section references an external 'cargo-fuzz' tool skill — both are named but not present in this skills repo (may be separate tool-skill packages or stubs).

skillReports.scope_claim: Exclusively the SolidStats `web` repo (TanStack Start / React / TSX). SKILL.md explicitly says "before writing any TS/TSX in `web`" and lists a locked stack. Claims no rules over server-2, replays-fetcher, or replay-parser-2.

sections.title: FSD Architecture: root layers, UI layers, slices/entrypoints
sections.gist: Three root layers (routes / pages / shared), eight UI sub-layers (pages/widgets/composites/actions/displays/layouts/wrappers/lib), PascalCase slice folders with index.ts public surfaces, layer-suffix naming, uikit-vs-feature boundary. Explicitly derived from estesis FSD but retargeted to TanStack Start; not applicable to other SolidStats repos.

sections.title: Component shape: named functions, props order, server/client boundary, icons
sections.gist: Named-function components with typed Props, system-props-first ordering, useCallback for handlers, explicit JSX ternaries, server-vs-client boundary per TanStack Start, Lucide-only icons, type='button' default. The server/client boundary split is TanStack Start-specific; naming and props-order rules are broadly React but the file encodes them as web-repo rules.

sections.title: Data flow: TanStack Query + Router loader-prefetch, openapi-fetch typed client, queryOptions factories
sections.gist: Loaders prefetch into the Query cache via ensureQueryData; components read with useQuery on the same key. All server access through openapi-fetch + openapi-react-query typed by generated paths from server-2's OpenAPI schema. No raw fetch, no hand-written DTOs, per-domain queryOptions factories, explicit staleTime/gcTime per family, list→detail→back contract.

sections.title: State boundaries: URL / Query / Nano Stores / ephemeral
sections.gist: Each state type has exactly one home: shareable state in typed Router search params (single source of truth), server data in TanStack Query cache only, client-only persistent state in Nano Stores, transient in component/Router. Violations are the primary cause of the back-nav and CLS bugs the brief forbids.

sections.title: Routing: typed TanStack Router, search params, scroll restoration, auth gates, /ru /en routes
sections.gist: File-based routes in src/routes, thin route files, validateSearch via zod/v4-mini, scroll + virtualization restoration, auth/role gates in beforeLoad before data loads, localized /ru /en prefixes with canonical + hreflang. All TanStack Router-specific.

sections.title: Localization: typed ICU i18n, const ln aliasing, /ru /en, hydration safety
sections.gist: Typed ICU-capable i18n, RU+EN from the start with /ru /en route prefixes, structured domain/layer keys, const ln aliasing convention (adapted from estesis), hydration-safe date/number serialization. RU+EN requirement and the specific aliasing convention are web-repo specific.

sections.title: TypeScript: generated OpenAPI types as source of truth, backend-enum Record safety, zod/v4-mini, type-fest/es-toolkit/dayjs/nanoid
sections.gist: type over interface, no any/!/unexplained as, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, generated OpenAPI paths as the single DTO source, Model→Data boundary, Record<Enum,…> for backend-driven maps, runtime validation via zod/v4-mini, type-fest for type-level utilities, es-toolkit for collection helpers, dayjs for dates, nanoid for client-side IDs. The strictness flags and no-any/no-interface rules are owned by solidstats-process-ts-standards; this file adds the web-specific generated-types and utility rules. Substantial overlap with ts-standards baseline.

sections.title: Toolchain: Vite+ (Oxlint + Oxfmt + tsgo) lint/format/type-check gate
sections.gist: vp check (Vite+ CLI) runs Oxlint + Oxfmt + tsgo configured in vite.config.ts; warnings are CI errors; suppressions need a comment. This toolchain choice is specific to the web repo (server-2 and replays-fetcher likely use different tooling).

sections.title: Styling: vanilla-extract file naming, token/theme contract, design direction rules
sections.gist: Colocated <ComponentName>Style.css.ts files, token-driven theme contract (dark default + light), semantic tokens only (no raw hex), clsx composition, no transition: all, stable dimensions for CLS, Lucide-only icons, design direction (no nested cards/ornamental gradients). vanilla-extract is a stack choice shared with estesis; the token schema and design direction are web-repo specific.

sections.title: Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard/focus, Ark UI primitives, live regions, touch targets
sections.gist: WCAG 2.2 AA minimum, full keyboard support via Ark UI headless primitives, visible focus, skip links + landmarks, one H1, 4.5:1/3:1 contrast, 44×44 touch targets, live regions for SSE without focus theft, focus management on route change. Ark UI is a web-stack choice; WCAG principles are universal but rules here are encoded specifically for the React/Ark stack.

sections.title: Performance & CWV: LCP/INP/CLS budgets, bundle splits, virtualization, render stability
sections.gist: LCP ≤ 2.5s / INP ≤ 200ms / CLS ≤ 0.02 budgets; route-level code splitting; reserved dimensions for async content; LCP in initial SSR HTML; virtualization for 10k–100k rows; render-stable props; transform/opacity animations with prefers-reduced-motion; bundle budgets in CI. CWV targets are universal doctrine; the implementation rules are React/TanStack-specific.

sections.title: Rendering & SEO: SSR for indexable pages, titles/meta/canonical, sitemaps, structured data, crawl-trap avoidance
sections.gist: SEO-critical public pages SSR-rendered before JS; unique title/meta/canonical; /ru /en hreflang; VideoGame/BreadcrumbList/ItemList structured data; segmented sitemap index for replay pages; curated indexable filter URLs + noindex for volatile states. The specific surface list (players/squads/rotations/commander/bounty/replays), the RU/EN pair, and structured data types are repo-specific.

sections.title: Realtime: SSE-first, per-page merge discipline, connection/stale states
sections.gist: SSE by default (WebSocket only for client→server live), no-surprise updates (no viewport reorder/CLS), per-page auto-merge vs explicit-confirm policy, visible reconnect/offline/timeout/stale states. The per-page merge discipline and stale-label convention are repo-specific product decisions.

sections.title: Errors: stable error codes, recovery copy taxonomy, request/form states, route error boundaries
sections.gist: Stable unique error codes from server-2 API, UI maps codes to localized copy (never raw string), user-action errors vs app/server errors with contact path + request id, all server-2 request states handled (validation/duplicate/cooldown/rate-limit/rejection), route error boundaries with recovery action. Stable codes are a universal doctrine; the server-2-specific state list is repo-specific.

sections.title: Tests: Playwright for components/journeys, Vitest for hooks/logic, CI gate
sections.gist: Playwright covers components and critical journeys (list→detail→back, SSE, a11y via axe); Vitest covers hooks and pure logic; no RTL tests. CI gates: full browser/viewport matrix, axe a11y, console errors, scroll/cache/CLS regressions, Lighthouse/budget, vp check. The Playwright-for-components (not RTL) mandate and the specific CI gate set are web-repo specific.

sections.title: Domain rules: players/squads/rotations/bounty/replays, slug model, provenance, request flows, moderation, RBAC
sections.gist: Slug-only current-owner player/squad routes, replay routes by ID, server-driven pagination for 10k-100k row tables, SteamID masked to last 4, bounty formula breakdown, guided request steppers (identity/kills/teamkills/remove-from-replay/commander-dispute), server-2 draft resources with 7-day TTL, immutable audit timeline, RBAC by roles + explicit capabilities. Entirely web-repo and SolidStats product-specific.

sections.title: Security: SSR server CSP/headers, env/secrets discipline, file upload validation
sections.gist: Node SSR server sets CSP (nonce-based preferred) + HSTS + XCTO + frame-ancestors via TanStack Start middleware; secrets server-only, never at module scope in client-reachable code; env validated at startup with zod/v4-mini; uploads validated by magic bytes not MIME, EXIF stripped, SVG disallowed; external links with noopener noreferrer. Some rules (no secrets in client bundles) are universal; the TanStack Start middleware integration is stack-specific.

sections.title: Forms: TanStack Form for request steppers, live-after-submit validation, draft autosave
sections.gist: TanStack Form for all multi-field inputs, one form instance per stepper, zod/v4-mini schema validator, live-after-submit revalidation (not on-keystroke before first submit), narrow field subscription, drafts autosaved to server-2 resource via debounced mutation. LAYERING PATTERN

The family uses a strict three-tier naming convention encoded directly in the skill slug: `{project}-{domain}-{stack}-{role}`. The first segment (`estesis`) is the project/org namespace. The second segment (`backend`, `process`) is the domain — whether the skill is tied to a runtime stack or to a cross-cutting workflow. The third segment, when present (`fastapi`, `csharp`, `react`, `swagger-spec`), identifies the specific technology stack, keeping stack knowledge out of the shared layers. The final segment names the role: `conventions` for the authoritative ruleset, `code-review` for the reviewer that enforces it, and `review-standards` for the foundation both depend on.

The shared-standards skill (`estesis-process-review-standards`) knows nothing about any stack; it owns only the review contract — severity scale, output format, verdict rules, and scope discipline. Every per-stack reviewer hard-requires it and reads it first, meaning the output format is always identical regardless of language or review type. The per-stack conventions skill (`estesis-backend-fastapi-vc-conventions`) is a pure reference — it has no procedural logic; it just owns stable-lettered rules. The per-stack reviewer then sits above both, reading conventions + standards and adding only what is stack-specific: the spec/tracker requirements gate and the design-quality checks (§T–§AB) reserved in the conventions skill's letter namespace. This makes the reviewer thin — most of its content is delegation.

The feedback skill (`estesis-process-review-feedback`) is a second-order process tool: it does not review code at all; it improves the reviewers by routing corrections back to exactly the right skill (or to the shared standards if the signal is general). The rule-of-three threshold and the two-stage capture/promote split prevent single-data-point noise from polluting the ruleset prematurely.

The SolidStats family (`solidstats-process-project-standards`, `solidstats-process-ts-standards`) borrowed the `{project}-{domain}-{role}` naming structure directly — using `solidstats` as the namespace and `process` as the domain for cross-cutting standards. It also adopted the pattern of separating a shared baseline (project-standards) from a stack-specific layer (ts-standards), mirroring how `estesis-process-review-standards` underpins the stack-specific reviewers. What SolidStats does not yet have (compared to the mature estesis family) is the reviewer tier itself, the feedback/learning loop, and the explicit §-lettered citation contract between conventions and reviewer skills.
